title: Designing in black and white first
excerpt: Why I start almost every project without color. Stripping a design down to greyscale makes hierarchy and spacing do the heavy lifting.
content: Color is persuasive. It can make a weak layout feel finished before it is ready. Starting in black and white forces the structure, hierarchy, and spacing to carry the experience. Once those decisions work, color becomes a useful layer instead of a rescue plan.

title: Making the web feel instant
excerpt: Practical performance wins, from preconnect and lazy loading to shipping less JavaScript on the first visit.
content: Perceived speed starts with a fast first frame. I look at the critical request chain, reserve media space before it loads, and keep interaction code close to the moment it is needed.

title: Accessibility is not optional
excerpt: A friendly checklist I run through on every build so the web works for more people, not just some people.
content: Keyboard navigation, visible focus, useful labels, readable contrast, and sensible heading order are not polish. They are the product working as intended.

title: CSS that scales with you
excerpt: How I structure stylesheets and use custom properties so a design system grows without turning into spaghetti.
content: A small set of intentional tokens, component boundaries, and layout primitives can take a stylesheet a long way. Complexity should be visible, named, and easy to change.
